screens_reviewed: Single capture of the audit wizard step 1 (Context) for 'Maple Library Plaza' in the DARK theme: 09-audit-context.png. Shows the Stack header, step pill, step-progress card, 9 step navigation pills, and the start of the 'Visit details' card (read-only auditor ID + audit date, first context question), plus the fixed Back / Save / Next footer.
verdict: This is the dark capture, yet the entire scrollable body renders the cream/light palette while only the native Stack header strip is dark — a hard theme bug caused by the route importing the static light-bound `designSystem` constant instead of `useDesignSystem()`. The layout, hierarchy, and spacing are otherwise well composed and on-brand, but the broken dark theme is disqualifying for a low-light field tool whose entire selling point is dark-mode legibility.

critical_issues.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx body (Card, StepHeader, footer) vs native header
critical_issues.issue: In the dark capture the whole audit body renders the cream light palette (cream background #FBFAF6, white cards, dark navy text) while the native Stack header above it renders dark (#24261F surfaceMuted with light text). The screen ignores the user's dark preference entirely. The route binds every color to the module-level `designSystem` constant, which is hard-wired to `lightColors`; it never subscribes to the resolved theme. Every sibling that reads `useDesignSystem()` (the header via useYeeStackHeaderOptions / YeeStackHeaderTitle) correctly goes dark, producing the split-palette seam visible between the header and the 'Step 1 of 9' pill.
critical_issues.evidence: image (dark header strip over cream body); app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:23 `import { designSystem } from "lib/design-system";` (static, not the hook); core.md:453-460 `export const designSystem = { colors: lightColors, ... }`; contrast: header uses useYeeStackHeaderOptions.ts:1994-2016 which calls useDesignSystem() and renders dark
critical_issues.fix: Replace the static import with `const designSystem = useDesignSystem();` inside AuditStepScreen and thread the resolved tokens into the child components (StepHeader, Card, FooterNav, getSurveyPalette, getStepTone) instead of referencing the module constant. getSurveyPalette/getStepTone must accept a `colors` argument (like getMetricTone in core.md:528) rather than closing over the static light palette.

critical_issues.issue: Even after switching the screen to useDesignSystem(), getSurveyPalette() and getStepTone() read `designSystem.colors.*` from the static light module constant, so card/inner/selected/intro surfaces and the step-pill tones would still resolve to light values. getStepTone also hardcodes a literal `border: "rgba(16, 35, 31, 0.16)"` (a dark-navy alpha tuned for cream) that will not read on a dark surface.
critical_issues.evidence: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1787-1805 (getSurveyPalette closes over static designSystem); :1774-1782 (getStepTone, literal rgba border)
critical_issues.fix: Pass the resolved `colors` (from useDesignSystem) into getSurveyPalette(step, colors) and getStepTone(step, colors); replace the literal rgba border with a token such as colors.border or colors.primarySoft so it tracks the active theme.

improvements.issue: The 9 step pills (Context / Weighting / Access / ...) are rendered as Buttons with py="$2" and fontSize 11. As secondary jump-to-step controls they read small; verify they meet the ~44pt iOS minimum height. minWidth is set to 108 but height is only padding-driven.
improvements.suggestion: Give the step pills an explicit minHeight (~44) or increase vertical padding so each pill is comfortably tappable, especially since they are the only way to jump between steps.

improvements.issue: 'Step 1 of 9' appears three times in the same viewport: the top pill, the 'Audit progress / Step 1 of 9' card, and the row of 9 named pills below it. This is redundant and consumes most of the first screen before the actual form (Visit details) is reached, pushing the first real question near the fold on a phone.
improvements.suggestion: Collapse the standalone 'Step 1 of 9' pill or the 'Audit progress' card into the named-pill row (the active pill already conveys position), freeing vertical space so the form starts higher on iPhone.

improvements.issue: Three flex=1 buttons (Back / Save & exit / Next) share one row inside screenPaddingHorizontal=15. On a compact iPhone width the 'Save…' label is already truncated in the capture, and each button's tappable width is narrow for a primary CTA.
improvements.suggestion: Consider stacking Save & exit onto its own line on narrow widths, or shorten labels, so the primary Next CTA gets adequate thumb width and 'Save & exit' is not truncated.
improvements.evidence: image ('Save…' truncated); app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1683-1717 (three flex=1 Buttons in one XStack)

tamagui_notes: The route opts out of the design system's theming entirely by importing the static `designSystem` (core.md:453) rather than the `useDesignSystem()` hook (core.md:501); this is the single source of the dark-mode failure and also means font-scale and dyslexic-font preferences are ignored on this screen (the hook also wires fontScale/dyslexicFont, core.md:502-509).

Heavy use of inline `style={{ ... }}` with raw color strings and literal rgba values (e.g. getStepTone border, app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1776) bypasses Tamagui theme tokens, which is what allows the static light palette to leak through regardless of theme.

design_system_components_used is (none): the screen hand-rolls Card, Badge-like pills, progress bar, and selection rows from raw YStack/XStack/Text instead of shared ui/* primitives (e.g. components/ui/Badge.tsx exists in core.md:1551). Routing these through theme-aware primitives would have prevented the light/dark leak.
platform_notes: Top safe area: the native Stack header (headerShown via useYeeStackHeaderOptions) sits under the Dynamic Island and renders correctly dark, so the notch inset is handled by the header; the cream body begins below it. No content is clipped by the island.

Bottom safe area: FooterNav applies paddingBottom={insets.bottom + 12} (app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:1680), and the scroll content reserves footerHeight + 48 bottom padding (:435), so the home indicator and fixed footer are handled correctly.

Thumb reach: the primary Next CTA is bottom-right in the fixed footer — good for right-thumb reach — but shares the row with two other flex=1 buttons, narrowing its hit area (see footer-three-buttons-cramped).
Compact-fit: the screen uses lib/responsive-layout via getResponsiveContentContainerStyle and layout.screenPaddingHorizontal rather than hardcoded values, which is correct for iPhone.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios within the (wrongly light) palette — the bug itself is the finding; ratios of the intended dark palette can't be judged from a capture that never rendered it.
Behavior of the selected/affirmative states, condition follow-ups, autosave toast, and the Alert confirm dialog — none are shown in this single static capture.
Whether the split-palette seam also affects later steps (2-9) or only step 1 — only step 1 was captured (though the static import is shared, so it almost certainly affects all steps).
score_rationale: Per the rubric, a screen that renders the wrong theme palette in its primary low-light use case is a significant, off-spec defect, not minor polish. The composition, spacing, and safe-area handling are genuinely solid (would be 7-8 if themed correctly), but the dark capture showing a cream body with a dark header is a clear, verifiable break (app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:23 + core.md:453) that lands this in the 3-4 'multiple significant problems' band.
